name: identity-stability
description:
The regression lock on the foreign id. This is the same device as the SCADA server in the happy scenario -- same uid -- after everything mutable about it has moved: both NICs readdressed, one MAC replaced, a hostname learned where there was none, device_name changed, the site renamed, the risk level raised, and a second Claroty asset_id issued. The emitted id must be byte-for-byte the id happy asserts, because none of those values may reach it.

That matters more here than for most sources. xDome retains a device's historical addressing on the same row rather than creating a new one, which is precisely why the vendor's uid is trusted for identity and why the ids asserted here and in happy have to be identical. check_determinism additionally re-runs the scenario on a fresh ephemeral port: the id carries no host component, so the port cannot leak into it. The second ip_list entry carries the documented ' / (Last Known IP)' annotation and is no longer imported as an address -- it is historical, not current -- so only the first MAC/IP pair appears in macPairs while both MACs survive as interfaces.
